questions.prompt: Which belt profile is mainly used for light-duty low-cost drives?
questions.explanation: The slide describes round belts as inexpensive and suited to light loads where slip and efficiency are less critical.

reviewCue.text: Review C210 Mechanical Power Sys.pdf, slide 110. The slide describes round belts as inexpensive and suited to light loads where slip and efficiency are less critical.
reviewCue.excerpt:
Five Types of Belt Drives and Give an Application of Each
The flat belt was the first type of belt drive used. Less common now but has 
been in use for 100s of years. Still found in conveyors, machine tools, printing 
presses, and textile machinery. Most common use is as a conveyor belt.
The round belt uses a circular cross- section. It is mainly found in very light duty 
applications, such as vacuums and printers, where either the load is light or 
slip and efficiency are not important. Its main asset is low cost.
The ribbed belt has ribs that run longitudinally (along the length) on the belt. 
These ribs are designed to seat in mating grooves in the sheaves.
This type of belt has a greater area of the belt in contact with the sheave, 
which means that there is less wear on the belt or sheaves.
The sheaves are more compact and higher pulley ratios can be used, typically 
as high as 40:1

reviewCue.excerpt:
Five Types of Belt Drives and Give an Application of Each
The V-belt is a wedge-shaped belt made from a combination of rubber and textile 
material. It became popular because of its advantages over flat belts:
⮚ Can operate at higher speeds.
⮚ Can transmit power more efficiently.
⮚ Can transmit power in a smaller size.
⮚ Requires very little maintenance.
The V-belt is designed to ride high in the groove gripping the walls of the pulley by 
wedging itself against the sides of the pulley groove as the belt is tightened.
Timing belts, which have notches or teeth, are used when slippage can’t be allowed in 
the drive train. As the drive pulley turns, its teeth engage the teeth of the belt and pull it. 
With this design, this belt does not slip, and a constant speed is maintained at the shaft.

questions.prompt: How does a V-belt transmit force to a sheave?
questions.answer: Friction enhanced by wedging in the groove
options: Friction enhanced by wedging in the groove
A shaft key inside the belt
questions.explanation: Tension seats the belt in the groove so wedging increases grip and power transmission.

reviewCue.text: Review C210 Mechanical Power Sys.pdf, slide 114. Tension seats the belt in the groove so wedging increases grip and power transmission.
reviewCue.excerpt:
V-belt drives transmit power between two sheaves with tension created on the belt. This tension 
causes the belt to be pulled down, or wedged, into the groove of the sheave, creating enough 
friction to keep the belt from slipping when the turning sheave is placed under a load.
How V-Belts Work and Wear
The wedging action of the V-belt creates friction between the sides of the sheave, not the 
groove bottom. The sides of the belt and sheave both wear and the belt gradually works its way 
down in the groove.
The V-belt should ride high in the groove, with its top near the top of the sheave. Normally, the 
V-belt does not touch the bottom of the sheave.

reviewCue.excerpt:
Runout
Set up the dial indicator and adjust it to the middle of its 
range. Rotate the shaft by hand and watch the indicator 
needle. Stop the rotation at the lowest reading and set the 
dial to "0". Rotate the shaft until the needle reads its 
highest. Subtract the highest from the lowest (usually 0”) to 
get the Total Indicator Reading, TIR.
Runout, is ½ of the total indicator reading.
A bent shaft or worn bearings will cause the shaft to 
wobble as it spins. This is called runout. It’s usually 
measured with a dial indicator as the spinning shaft 
moves up and down. If there is movement  (looseness) 
in the end of the shaft, that’s called end-float.
End Float
For labs, we will use typical values of 0.002” as 
maximums for runout and 0.001” for end float.

questions.prompt: What does the force-deflection method check?
questions.explanation: Apply the specified force at the span and compare deflection with the belt data; use the correct drive specification.

reviewCue.text: Review C210 Mechanical Power Sys.pdf, slide 119. Apply the specified force at the span and compare deflection with the belt data; use the correct drive specification.
reviewCue.excerpt:
Belt Tension – Force Deflection Method
Skill 2 - Determine the Belt Deflection Force for a Given Application
Belts need enough tension to avoid slippage while minimizing 
tension to avoid wear and tear.
Tension is measured by providing a known force and measuring the 
deflection:
⮚ Knowing the belt cross section and sheave diameter, use a 
table to pick a minimum force to apply.
⮚ Measure the belt span, which is the unsupported length.
⮚ Divide the belt span by 64 to get a target deflection.
⮚ At the center of the span, press the tension gauge to the 
target deflection and measure the force.
⮚ The force needs to be at least the minimum from the table, up 
to 50% more (1.5 times that).
⮚ If the force is out of range, loosen or tighten the belt to bring it 
into the range. 
Belt Tension Gauge

reviewCue.excerpt:
Four Types of Roller Chain Drives with Applications of Each
Single-strand chain are the most common roller chain used. A single 
row of rollers with plates on each side make up the chain.
Single-strand chains are used for most general-purpose applications of 
low-to- medium power transmissions. This type of chain is also found on 
bicycles.
Applications that transmit a great deal of power often use multiple-
strand chains. The chains used in multiple-strand chain drives are 
the same as those used in single-strand drives. They are merely 
joined to create multiple rows.
Multiple-strand chains are used in applications with much heavier 
loads and higher speeds than a single-strand chain can handle.

questions.prompt: How can chain sag be adjusted?
questions.answer: Move adjustable shaft centers or use a chain idler
options: Move adjustable shaft centers or use a chain idler
questions.explanation: Changing center distance or positioning an idler takes up slack while maintaining the prescribed sag.

reviewCue.text: Review C210 Mechanical Power Sys.pdf, slide 134. Changing center distance or positioning an idler takes up slack while maintaining the prescribed sag.
reviewCue.excerpt:
Two Methods Used to Adjust Chain Sag
In a system with adjustable centers, when the sag of a chain 
needs to be adjusted, the centers of the drive system can be 
moved either farther apart or closer together.
Another method used to adjust chain sag is with a device 
called a CHAIN IDLER. A CHAIN IDLER is a mechanism that has a 
small sprocket attached to an arm.
Some chain idler arms are spring-loaded, which automatically 
keeps constant tension in the chain drive via the idler sprocket.
If a spring-loaded arm is not used, the location of the idler 
sprocket must be manually adjusted to achieve the desired 
chain tension.

questions.prompt: What primarily causes a used roller chain to elongate?
questions.explanation: Wear increases spacing between links, making the chain longer. The slide specifies replacement at 3% elongation.

reviewCue.text: Review C210 Mechanical Power Sys.pdf, slide 135. Wear increases spacing between links, making the chain longer. The slide specifies replacement at 3% elongation.
reviewCue.excerpt:
Chains Do Not Stretch, They Wear and Elongate
Chain sag will need to be removed as it increases with time, making it look like the 
chain is stretching. The chain is not stretching; the bushings are wearing.
If a chain has 75 links, and the bushings each wear 0.010”, the chain will lengthen by 
75 X 0.010, or 0.75 inch. The wear just causes the space between individual links to 
increase in length.
It is important to understand that a chain 
should be replaced when its length 
becomes 3% longer than its original length.

Function and Operation of a Master Link
Some chain drives do not have adjustable centers; their shafts cannot be moved closer or farther 
apart. The chain must be separated and rejoined so it can be installed or removed.
This is done with a special chain link called a MASTER LINK, which is a standard link with one 
removable side plate. With the side plate removed, a master link can be inserted into a chain or 
removed from it. A cotter pin or a locking spring clip secures the removable side plate of a 
master link.
THE CLOSED END OF THE CLIP SHOULD POINT IN THE DIRECTION THE CHAIN MOVES, IN THE FIRST 2 
PHOTOS ABOVE THE CHAIN IS MOVING TO THE LEFT
